---
title: Tools and schemas
description: Design tools the model uses well, with zod (bundled) or JSON Schema (MCP) inputs, honest effects, data-only results and recoverable states.
icon: Wrench
---

Tools are a plugin's API, both for the model and for your own screens. A good tool is small, does
one thing, says exactly when to use it, and returns data the model can act on. The concepts live in
[Tools and effects](/en/docs/concepts/tools-and-effects); this page covers the practice.

## Naming

| Thing | Rule | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tool name | ASCII camelCase verb or noun, unique in the plugin | `cardBalance`, `search`, `reserveSeat` |
| Tool id | `<plugin>.<name>` (automatic) | `wallet.cardBalance` |
| Model name | `<plugin>__<name>` (automatic) | `wallet__cardBalance` |
| `title` | Short Chinese label for users | `校园卡余额` |

Every enabled tool is sent with every request, so fold related reads into one tool with a filter
argument instead of writing ten near-identical ones.

## Descriptions

`description` is for the model. Write it in English or Chinese, and cover:

- **When** to use it, in the words a student would use ("Use when the user asks which canteen is
  least crowded").
- **What** comes back: fields, units (yuan, minutes, Beijing time), how fresh the data is.
- **Limits** and **follow-ups**: page sizes, required order ("call `treehole__sendCode` first"),
  what to do on `verification_required`.

Don't repeat the input schema there. Describe the fields with `.describe()` instead.

When the text depends on the device, `description` can be a function of host services:

```ts
description: (services) => `Show a native UI in the chat… Components:\n${services.genui.describeCatalog()}`,
```

## Inputs

Bundled plugins use zod 4. The model sees the JSON Schema generated from it, and the host validates
every call (from the agent, a screen or the scheduler) before `execute` runs.

```ts
input: z.object({
  from: z.string().trim().max(20).optional().describe('boarding place, e.g. 燕园 / 新燕园'),
  at: z.string().optional().describe('Beijing time "YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm", default now'),
  count: z.number().int().min(1).max(10).optional().describe('departures per direction, default 3'),
}),
```

- Bound every number and string (`.min`, `.max`), and state defaults in the description.
- Use enums for closed sets (`z.enum(['weekday', 'holiday'])`).
- For times the model writes, use local `"YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm"` strings. The SDK's
  `scheduleInputSchema` and `parseLocal` already do this for schedules.
- Remote plugins: the device converts the MCP `inputSchema` (JSON Schema) to zod with
  `z.fromJSONSchema`, so stick to plain JSON Schema features.

## Effects

Each tool has exactly one effect: `read`, `write`, `money` or `public` (see
[Permissions](/en/docs/concepts/permissions)).

```ts
effect: 'read',      // a balance, a list, a search
effect: 'write',     // add a to-do, follow a post, book a room
effect: 'money',     // create a payment order, top up, switch the card to digital mode
effect: 'public',    // post or reply on Treehole
```

Set `untrusted: true` on tools that return third-party text, and `userOnly: true` on gates the
agent must not open itself.

## Results

```ts
execute: async ({ name, sort = 'least' }, ctx) => {
  const { time, canteens } = await fetchCrowd(ctx.signal);
  return { time, canteens: canteens.filter((c) => !name || c.name.includes(name)), source: CROWD_SOURCE };
},
```

- Return JSON objects whose field names and units explain themselves.
- When it matters, say where the data came from and how fresh it is (`source`, `time`).
- Return ids the model can pass to the next tool.
- Pass `ctx.signal` (abort) to network calls.
- On failure, throw an `Error` with a short Chinese message the user can read
  (`throw new Error('校园卡登录已失效')`). The agent relays it.
- When the user has to step in for an expected reason, return a status instead of throwing:

```ts
export type VerificationRequired = { status: 'verification_required'; kind: 'login'; methods: ['sms']; message: string };

// in execute:
if (needsSms) {
  return {
    status: 'verification_required',
    kind: 'login',
    methods: ['sms'],
    message: '树洞需要短信验证。先调用 treehole__sendCode 发送验证码，再带上 code 重试。',
  } satisfies VerificationRequired;
}
```

## Context and instructions

| Field | Sent | Use for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `instructions` | In the system prompt, every request | Short rules: which tool for which question, caveats ("以预约系统为准") |
| `context({ query, kv, services })` | Before each turn, marked as data (800 ms budget) | Facts relevant to this message, e.g. the memory snapshot. Return `undefined` when nothing applies. |

Both cost tokens on every request, and both change the prompt prefix, which hurts the model's
cache. Keep them short and stable. Leave out the time and date: the harness adds them to every turn.

## Calling your tools from UI

```ts
// in a screen or widget (actor: 'user', no approval prompt)
await invoke('focus.start', { label: '高数' });

// live read with the host's shared cache
const data = host.useToolData<{ minutes: number }>('focus.today', {}, { ttlMinutes: 1 });
```

## Checklist

- [ ] One responsibility per tool; reads and writes split.
- [ ] Chinese `title`, English title in `i18n.en.tools`, model-facing `description`.
- [ ] Every input field bounded and described.
- [ ] Honest `effect`; `untrusted` / `userOnly` where they apply.
- [ ] Results are data, small, with units; no secrets, no instructions.
- [ ] Errors are short user-readable messages; recoverable states are status objects.
